history.dynasty: Jaintia Kingdom (per temple-complex tradition; exact build date undocumented)
history.summary: FLAG ON CSV TOWN: the shrine is at Nartiang village in West Jaintia Hills district, NOT Jowai (Jowai is the district headquarters town, approx. 25 km away) - the CSV town is wrong. This is the Shiva temple that stands within walking distance of the famous Nartiang Durga Temple (one of the 51 Shakti Peethas; see seq 701 and 684 in this dataset): the Oh! Meghalaya site guide 'NARTIANG (DURGA AND SHIVA TEMPLES)' and the temple's Wikipedia-derived descriptions all describe a Shiva temple close to the Durga temple where 'one can see the remains of ancient cannons from the past inside the temple', and a recent visitor account identifies it as the Bhairava (Kamadishwar) temple housing idols of Kali and Durga with cannons in the background. The priests practising in the vicinity are described as direct descendants of the original priests who came from Jaintiapur (the old Jaintia capital). Identity is VERIFIED at the complex level but COARSE: no source gives this shrine a distinct name, builder or date separate from the Durga temple complex, so its individual antiquity and founding details are unrecorded - treat as a Jaintia-era shrine of the Nartiang sacred complex pending local documentation. Coordinates are approximate, set at the Durga temple (the Shiva shrine is within walking distance). No reliable image of this specific shrine was found after genuine searching (image results showed Assam cannons, not Nartiang), so media is intentionally empty.

name: Shiva Temple Nartiang
town_description: Nartiang is a historic village in West Jaintia Hills district, about 60-65 km east of Shillong on the Shillong-Jowai road. Once the summer capital of the Jaintia Kingdom, it is famous as the 'Garden of Monoliths' - scattered clusters of ancient Khasi-Jaintia menhirs and dolmens - and for the Nartiang Durga Temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Nearby attractions include Thadlaskein Lake and the district town of Jowai (~25 km).

travel.airport: Nearest airport with scheduled commercial flights: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 170-200 km by road; verify). Shillong (Umroi) airport is closer (approx. 85-95 km; verify) but has limited scheduled services (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station is the nearest major railhead (approx. 165-190 km by road; verify); onward by taxi or bus via Shillong/Jowai.
travel.road: Nartiang is approx. 60-65 km east of Shillong on the Shillong-Jowai road (NH-6) and approx. 25 km from Jowai (verify); reachable by taxi, shared sumo, and state buses from Shillong and Jowai.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Durga Puja (September-October) at the adjacent Durga temple is the most vibrant time to visit the complex.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx. 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily per traveller listings for the complex (verify - temple-managed hours are not published). No entry fee reported (verify). Dress modestly; the shrines follow Khasi-Jaintia customs alongside Hindu ritual.
